opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and sports marketing — up 8%, primarily on higher brand marketing.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — down 13%, as the year-ago quarter carried $340M of restructuring charges.

footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($12M) and Corporate (-$26M, mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: down 330 basis points, on discounts and inventory reserves

oneTimers: The effective tax rate was just 5.9%, versus 16.5% a year ago — Nike said a one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit from recently finalized U.S. tax regulations related to foreign-currency gains and losses flattered the quarter's bottom line.
otherDetail: $18M of net interest income, plus $38M of other income, net.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — footwear fell 9%, while apparel rose 7% and equipment 10%.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East and Africa — down 10% on reported numbers, down 6% without currency effects.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Asia-Pacific (outside Greater China) and Latin America — down 11% reported, down 4% without currency effects.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: China — the weakest region this quarter, with footwear and apparel each down 17%.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Converse sneaker brand — down across all territories.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global brand divisions plus corporate leftovers (mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.

takeaways.text: Revenue fell 9% to $11.3B (down 7% without currency effects). Nike Direct fell 12% as digital sales dropped 15%, wholesale fell 7%, and every geography declined — Greater China most, at -17%.
takeaways.title: Sales fell across the map

takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 330 basis points to 41.5%, primarily on higher discounts, higher inventory obsolescence reserves, higher product costs and changes in channel mix. Inventories ended down 2% at $7.5B.
takeaways.title: Discounts squeezed the margin

takeaways.text: Net income fell 32% to $794M and EPS to $0.54 — cushioned by the unusually low 5.9% tax rate. Operating overhead fell 13% because the year-ago quarter carried $340M of restructuring charges.
takeaways.title: Profit fell 32%

verdict: Nike's revenue fell 9% to $11.3B and profit dropped 32% to $794M under its 'Win Now' reset — discounts and inventory obsolescence reserves cut the gross margin by 330 basis points, partly cushioned by a one-time tax benefit.
